title: Mary at the hour of our death
word: Mary at the hour of our death
hook: every Hail Mary asks her prayer now and at the hour of our death
tomorrow: can thinking about death actually make you happier?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: my company, a crowd of saints that knows your name. Today, the one in that company whose prayer Catholics ask for in every Hail Mary.
screen: `MY COMPANY.` → `ONE NAME IN EVERY HAIL MARY.`

segments.voice: Hospital rooms at night have their own sounds: a machine that beeps, a cart in the hallway, somebody's TV through the wall. Families sit there and run out of words. When the words run out in a Catholic family, someone may start a Hail Mary. Nobody plans it. It's simply the words that are already there. And the prayer already knows where it is. Its last line asks Mary to pray for us now and at the hour of our death. Why there?
screen: `A HOSPITAL ROOM AT NIGHT.` → `THE WORDS RUN OUT.` → `NOW AND AT THE HOUR.`

segments.voice: Because she's been there. John's Gospel says, in the Douay-Rheims: "there stood by the cross of Jesus, his mother." She stood, and watched her son die. Then, from the cross, Jesus gives her away, to the disciple he loved: "Behold thy mother." And John says from that hour the disciple took her to his own. Catholics read that as a gift to every disciple. Now look at the prayer. Its first half is from Luke: the angel's greeting and Elizabeth's blessing. Its second half is the Church asking: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners. Then just two moments: now, and the hour of our death. Every other moment of your life fits between them. That's the surprise. A prayer people often say fast, for small things, has been rehearsing the biggest moment all along. Said every day, it means that when the hour comes, the words are already there, and so, Catholics trust, is she. Notice whose prayer is asked for: not a formula's, a mother's. Catholics ask Mary to pray with them, never to take God's place.
screen: `SHE STOOD BY THE CROSS.` · `BEHOLD THY MOTHER.` · `TWO HALVES, TWO MOMENTS.` · `REHEARSING THE LAST HOUR.` · then, large: `AT THE HOUR.`

segments.voice: Sit with your hands open on your knees. Pray one Hail Mary as slowly as you can, a breath for each phrase, and let the last line land: now, and at the hour. If that prayer isn't yours, sit with the face of someone you'd want beside you at the end.
Mary at the hour of our death. The mother who stood by the cross, asked to stand by ours.
screen: `MARY AT THE HOUR OF OUR DEATH — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: at the hour. She stood by the cross once, and Catholics trust she'll stand by ours. Go gently.

howItsDone: Catholics pray the Hail Mary daily, alone or in the rosary, and families often pray it at the bedside of someone who is dying.
